reason: H0 always calls BrotliDecoderCreateInstance(0, 0, 0), so it never exercises S1's custom allocator configuration or controlled allocation failures during decoding. This is fuzz-worthy because decoder-controlled input determines allocations such as context_map_size in DecodeContextMap, and S1 contains explicit allocation-error and cleanup paths whose state transitions are absent from H0.
evidence: BrotliDecoderCreateInstance selects malloc only when both alloc_func and free_func are null, and separately supports the alloc_func/free_func/opaque path.
DecodeContextMap allocates input-derived context_map_size through BROTLI_ALLOC(s, (size_t)context_map_size) and returns BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_ALLOC_CONTEXT_MAP when allocation returns 0.

BrotliDecoderDestroyInstance retrieves state->free_func and state->memory_manager_opaque before BrotliDecoderStateCleanup, making allocator/cleanup protocol behavior part of the exercised API surface.
recommended_action: Add a decoder fuzz mode using paired custom alloc_func/free_func callbacks with fuzzed or systematically enumerated allocation-failure points, then stream the same input through BrotliDecoderDecompressStream and always call BrotliDecoderDestroyInstance to cover partial-state cleanup.
